items.title: Ruth Lion interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 15, 1998
items.q: And then we got on the Steve Allen Show with the Jazz Messengers, which was very momentous, and very exciting.

ctx.x: How did you go about doing that? Was it through trying to get airplay and all that?

Airplay. Particularly. And I recall on the 25th anniversary of Blue Note, I had a lot of buddies who were radio people, and we invited them all, we had a party at The Playboy Club. And about three times more people than we invited, radio people came. But that was very indicative of the fact that the music was very popular. New York was very jazz oriented at that time. And so you had no trouble — I’d take the artist to the programs and — I’ve forgotten the first coast to coast program we had, who did we have —…
Let’s talk about Art Blakey for a minute.
